newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Lebanon PM asks Europe to press Israel on peace.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon PM asks Europe to press Israel on peace.

text.p: Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri urged European states on Friday to put economic pressure on Israel to remove its forces from south Lebanon and break a deadlock in the stalled peace process.

"We hope the international community will put pressure on Israel to withdraw from our territory," Hariri told an international business forum in the Swiss mountain resort of Crans Montana in a live satellite link from Beirut.
"Europe has an interest in seeing the peace process going ahead and they have to do something about it," he said.
"Israel has strong economic relations with Europe. Europe can play an important role if it tried to put pressure on Israel to convince it to go ahead with the peace process."
The U.N. Security Council has called for Israel's unconditional withdrawal from a 15-km (nine miles)-wide anti-guerrilla buffer strip it has occupied in south Lebanon since 1978.
"The Arabs are ready for peace, the Lebanese are ready, the only one who doesn't believe in peace is Israel," Hariri said.
"Netanyahu is blocking peace. The Israelis have to find a way out to continue the peace process. Netanyahu has to decide, Israel has to decide, if they want to live in peace in the region."

Hariri also said he regretted the position of United States, which has blocked condemnation of Israel at the United Nations over its work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem that has deadlocked the Middle East peace process since March.
But he said he hoped U.S. President Bill Clinton "is interested in peace and will put real pressure on Israel so Israel will go ahead with the peace process."
